entries.claim: Death-band gate on CI (6 cases x 3 replicates, 18 episodes per arm): suite totals base 122.333 placed / 110.587 fill vs gate 125.667 / 119.501, i.e. +3.33 placed and +8.91 fill, roughly twice the null-pair noise floor measured in the same session (1.7 placed / 3.9 fill). Per-case, however, the local story does NOT reproduce: c000-k1 gains most (+4.667 placed, +10.13 fill) where locally the gate never fired, while m2-k15 -- the two-container scene that carried the entire local case (+8.5 mean) -- comes back at -1.667 placed on CI. c001-k1 is unchanged (+0.0/+0.335), b000-k15 -1.0, b000-k20 +0.667, b001-k20 +0.667. The direction of the aggregate is positive and above noise; the per-case attribution measured locally is not supported. Faster CI hardware changes which turns land in the death band, so which scene benefits is hardware-dependent -- the mechanism (do not execute a release your own model prices at P_rot>=0.5 when a safer candidate exists) is what generalises, not the per-case magnitudes.
entries.source: CI run 30865594779 aggregate (Death-band ablation, ref claude/l3-l4-allocation-ordering)

entries.claim: Common random numbers were genuinely missing from the MC rollout comparison (seed=rank scored every branch against a different set of 24 sampled futures) and fixing it does NOT revive the method: Spearman(mc, placed) moves -0.344 -> -0.295 on the same labelled step-10 branches, still indistinguishable from zero and still the wrong sign, with the best branch (+11) scoring mid-pack. The defect was real; it was not the cause. This SUPERSEDES my in-conversation retraction of the earlier closure -- the closure was correct, and it is now better supported because the instrument carries a variance-reduction control it previously lacked. What the residual negative sign suggests, untested: a geometric floor-filling rollout rewards flat well-packed boards, which is not what the deadline-driven policy needs, so the proxy may be anti-correlated with the target by construction rather than merely noisy. The remaining conditional-probability line that does not depend on rollout fidelity is a learned survival model P(reach step t+k | placement features), trainable on the horizon labels and CI traces already generated, with near-zero inference cost.

A logistic termination-hazard model fitted on the policy traces already in the repository (309 runs, 6293 decisions, 9 cases, horizon 3 steps, 17 decision-time features, no sklearn) is the first thing measured in this workstream to discriminate WITHIN an episode position. Headline numbers are misleading and are recorded here so they cannot be quoted alone: LOSO mean AUC 0.945, but step_index ALONE scores 0.944 -- essentially the whole pooled AUC is the tautology that late decisions are near the end. The load-bearing number is within-step discordant-pair accuracy over 19254 pairs: 0.644 with all features, 0.615 with step_index removed, against 0.5 chance. Every previous candidate in this workstream (board-value counts, Phi, MC rollout value) produced either zero comparable pairs or chance-level accuracy. Structural limitation that bounds the use: the features describe the SEARCH that produced a decision (unit coverage, accept rates, rejection profile, attempts), not a specific candidate pose, so this cannot tie-break between candidates at one board -- and the pairs measured are same-step-different-trajectory, not same-board-different-action. Its legitimate use is as a state-level trigger, e.g. replacing the death-band gate's fitted -1.5 score constant with a LOSO-validated hazard threshold.
entries.source: scripts/fit_hazard_model.py; reports/hazard/hazard-h3.json; feature ablation and within-step stratification run 2026-08-04

entries.claim: The death-band gate REGRESSED the official score by 15.3% and is reverted to default OFF. submissiondeathband 29.959 against submissiontrueenvelope 35.375, with all six components down: cog -20.7%, stability -22.4%, soft -18.1%, placement -13.3%, fill -1.8%, num_placed -2.6%. Attribution is clean: the build differs from the 35.375 build by ~240 lines but nothing else changes default behaviour (tilt margin 0 makes its shrink an identity, both L3 knobs off, constructive order unchanged, lateral guard unchanged). Two lessons, both checkable in advance and both missed. (1) The mechanism was implied by Ranker.score: the score the gate overrides is +2.0*support +0.35y -0.18*z*mass, the only terms steering cog and stability, so preferring lower-scored placements spends exactly the components that fell hardest. (2) The warning was already in local data -- every ablation row carries shake_response, and on m2-k15, the case whose +8.5 placed justified shipping, the gate arm was WORSE on every stability proxy: peak kinetic energy 25.59 -> 44.64 (+74%), max shift 0.3189 -> 0.4241 (+33%), items shifted 7.00 -> 8.38. final_com_z moved the other way (0.754 -> 0.704, nominally better) and was wrong, so the shake proxy is the one to trust. This is also the first measured instance of the gate multiplier acting DOWNWARD: -2.6% placed produced -20.0% across the four gated components, an amplification of 7.6x against the 6.7x measured upward.
entries.source: Official feedback for submissiondeathband vs submissiontrueenvelope; local shake audit over death-band-v2/ and death-band-scenes/ rows; AGENT_OPERATIONS.md section 5.05

entries.claim: A shake-inclusive acceptance criterion would have blocked the death-band regression, and is now wired into the runner everyone reads. Retrospective test on all local base-vs-gate runs (base n=23, gate n=29): placed/fill alone say ADOPT (20.6 -> 23.2 placed, 18.8 -> 20.5 fill), which is the judgement actually made; adding the shake proxy says REJECT (max shift 0.209 -> 0.230, peak kinetic energy 17.00 -> 19.56, items shifted 4.78 -> 4.86, all worse), which matches the official answer (35.375 -> 29.959). run_risk_ablation --summarize now aggregates and prints the three shake columns; previously it printed final_com_z as the only non-official stand-in, and that one pointed the WRONG way on the same pair. The repository already had an aggregator for these (scripts/analyze_stability_tradeoff.py) and four stand-in proxies that no measurement-registry entry described; all are now registered with cannot_answer, including the recorded directional falsifications of final_com_z and priority_clean_ratio. Caveat that bounds this: exactly one controlled official pair supports the shake proxy's direction, the shake protocol magnitudes are invented so only same-config arm comparisons carry meaning, and the one paired study on these axes reached no significant sign test.
entries.source: scripts/run_risk_ablation.py summarize wiring; retrospective on scratchpad death-band-v2 and death-band-scenes rows; context/measurements.json instrument entries for evaluator.py and diagnostics.py

entries.claim: The shake proxy cannot serve as a per-run acceptance veto: its own repeat-to-repeat noise exceeds the effect it was credited with catching. Across 20 (case, arm) cells with repeated identical runs, the median relative spread between identical repeats is 22.7% for shake_max_shift, 74.6% for shake_peak_kinetic_energy and 42.9% for shake_items_shifted, against a death_band-vs-base gap of +10.0%, +15.1% and +1.7%. All three 'signals' therefore sit inside the noise, and the three metrics are correlated measurements of one shake, so agreeing in direction is roughly one to two coin flips, not three. My previous entry claiming a shake-inclusive criterion would have blocked the death-band regression is superseded: the direction was right by luck, not by resolution. What remains usable: pooled comparison over many paired runs (at n~25 per arm the standard error of the mean is roughly 8-15%, so the observed 15% gap is one to two SE -- suggestive, not significant), never a single run and never a single case. The design consequence taken instead of trusting it: make a change unable to trade stability BY CONSTRUCTION rather than verifying afterwards with a proxy that cannot resolve the trade.
entries.source: within-cell spread audit over scratchpad death-band-v2, death-band-scenes, l3-route, l3-ablate, taskc-tilt rows

entries.claim: Death-band gate redesigned so the trade that cost the official score cannot occur by construction. v1 swapped to the best-scored candidate with P_rot < 0.5, buying lower toppling risk with whatever the replacement gave up -- support ratio, the physical quantity Ranker.score spends on cog and stability, which the official submission charged 20.7% and 22.4% for. v3 requires DOMINANCE: a replacement must be both safer on P_rot and no worse on support ratio than the action it replaces, otherwise the original action stands and the gamble is taken knowingly. No coefficients; it is a Pareto condition on two quantities the agent already computes. This route was chosen over verifying v1 with a local proxy because the audit showed the shake proxy cannot resolve the trade (repeat spread 23-75% against an effect of 2-15%). Knob DEATH_BAND_REQUIRE_DOMINANCE default on; arm death_band_v1 keeps the regressed behaviour measurable. The gate itself remains default OFF pending a submission. Six contract tests pin: ships off, dominance on, score band present and negative, budget floor positive, and that a lower-support replacement is rejected while an equal-support one is not.
entries.source: agent/agent.py death-band block; tests/test_death_band_gate.py; supersedes the mechanism analysed in death-band-official-regression-15pct

entries.claim: Each tightening of the death-band dominance condition roughly halves its firing rate on m2-k15, and the fully-guarded version is at the edge of being a no-op. Firings per episode, 2 repeats each: v1 (P_rot only, the version that regressed the official total 15.3%) 2 and 5; v3 (also requires support_ratio not worse) 3 and 2; v4 (also requires z*mass not higher) 2 and 0. The structural finding is that dominance-satisfying replacements DO exist -- v1's official loss was avoidable by design rather than unavoidable -- but the fully-guarded gate acts on at most a couple of turns per episode, so its upside is bounded by construction. Placed counts across these runs (v3 29/31, v4 31/14) are not usable: m2-k15 base alone spans 18-27 and this is n=2, and the shake proxy has already been shown unable to resolve differences of this size. The honest consequence is that v4 cannot be evaluated locally at all -- only a submission could -- while its bounded upside makes that a poor use of a submission compared with first restoring the 35.375 configuration, which the trunk does not currently contain.
entries.source: scratchpad dbv3/ and dbv4/ firing counts on m2-k15

entries.claim: Two instrument defects in the Task A rollout path, both found while trying to replay submitted agents for score calibration, and both of which contaminated earlier results. (1) run_task_a_rollout.py set case_id = next(iter(config)), so --source-case was written into the row but never applied: every rollout ran case 000 regardless. (2) sync_agent_into_simulator() overwrote simulator/agent.py from the working tree unconditionally, so an attempt to measure a previously submitted build silently measured the current one -- four runs of two different agents on two nominally different cases returned byte-identical fill, placed, com_z and shake. Both are fixed: the case is selected explicitly and written to a single-case config, and the sync honours AGENT_PATH. Consequence for the record: the constructive-order ablation reported as '2 cases x 2 modes x 3 repeats' was in fact ONE case with 6 repeats per mode. Its numbers still do not overlap (composite 22,22,23,22,23,24 vs volume-only 20,21,21,20,20,20), so the direction survives, but the claimed case diversity did not exist and that entry is superseded by this one.
entries.source: scripts/run_task_a_rollout.py and scripts/run_risk_ablation.py fixes; identical-output evidence in scratchpad calib/

entries.claim: The score-calibration plan does not work as designed, for a reason worth recording: the two submissions that differ by 15.3% officially are nearly indistinguishable on our local cases. Replaying both submitted agent.py builds (sha bcd72b3a = trueenvelope 35.375, sha 4988f258 = deathband 29.959) on the two distributed cases as Task A gives IDENTICAL fill (33.124 / 20.268), identical placed (0.561 / 0.381) and identical com_z (0.7302 / 0.7853); only shake_max_shift moves at all, by 2.8% on case 000 and not at all on case 001. So the official 15.3% gap is generated on cases we do not have -- the rules state the evaluation uses entirely different test cases -- and no proxy-to-component mapping can be identified from replaying submissions on this suite. What this does establish, and it is the more useful finding: the distributed two-case suite has almost no discriminating power for a selection change that officially costs 15.3%, which is a property of the suite rather than of the proxies. The consequence for future work is to invest in local cases that resemble the official ones (multi-container, larger streams, priority containers) rather than in more proxies measured on cases that cannot separate the builds.
entries.source: scratchpad calib2/ replay of both submitted builds after the source-case and agent-sync fixes

entries.claim: submissiontrueenvelope scores 35.37542828677423, against 23.245587753037217 and 17.58143419644042 -- the total has exactly DOUBLED over three submissions (+101.2%), and this step alone is +52.2%. It fixes a y-axis error in the anchor envelope (22b88d2 cherry-pick, 3b1635c). All six components rose again: fill 31.413 -> 34.246, cog 21.505 -> 40.683, stability 29.424 -> 53.240, placement 10.850 -> 16.950, soft 12.650 -> 21.300, num_placed 0.452 -> 0.505. Timing unchanged at 149.19 s and 6.55 s. THE NEW FINDING IS THAT THE GATE AMPLIFICATION IS DECAYING. From sub22 to 3334 a 4.2% placed gain produced 58.2% on the four gated components, about 14x; from 3334 to trueenvelope an 11.6% placed gain produced 77.6%, 6.7x. The pass-fraction lower bound rises 0.207 -> 0.294 -> 0.532. Halving leverage is the signature of the cutoff saturating: as fewer cases remain below it, further placed gains stop earning the multiplier and what is left is conditional quality. A placed-only strategy therefore has an expiry, which is visible for the first time here. The original section-4 conclusion survives all three observations and is now better supported, because a higher f tightens the bounds: at f >= 0.532, E[placement|pass] <= 31.8 and E[soft|pass] <= 40.0 against E[cog|pass] <= 76.4. Conditional on clearing the gate, placement and soft are still the two worst components.
entries.source: Official feedback for submissiontrueenvelope.zip, 2026-08-03, against the submission3334 and submission22 logs. Comparison table and the decaying-amplification argument in docs/OFFICIAL_SCORE_LOG.md.
entries.caveats: Three observations, and consecutive submissions differ by more than one change, so no component delta is attributable to a single commit. The amplification ratios are computed from mean placed fraction and the sum of the four gated components; both the cutoff value and the score weights remain unpublished, so this describes a trend in the platform's own numbers rather than a model of them. Two points do not establish a decay rate -- record the ratio for every future submission before acting on the crossover.

entries.claim: Three of the four container-configuration axes the competition declares had never been executed, and building a probe for them immediately found a hard crash. COMPETITION_RULES section 2 states every task is posed with combinations of one or two containers, shelf present or absent, empty or pre-loaded, and a priority-dedicated container present or absent; the official QA additionally forbids per-task submissions, so one agent must self-detect the setup and these branches WILL be taken. The bundled sample_config.json covers exactly one axis: both cases are single-container, empty, no dedicated container, differing only in the shelf, and the whole development suite derives from those two cases by changing look-ahead, so it inherits the same blind spot. First defect found: a two-container config built by copying the bundled camera block raises IndexError in env.reset() at env.py:318, because camera.num_containers sizes the shared depth-map array (env.py:80-88) and the bundled value is 1. That is a config-side defect rather than a simulator bug, but it is unavoidable for anyone who has never built a two-container scene. With it corrected the dual-dedicated-priority scene RUNS: placed fraction 0.732 (30 of 41), is_valid true, container usage 22 on index 0 and 9 on index 1, priority_misrouted 0 -- so multi-container placement and dedicated routing both work in physics for the first time. Two caveats on that number: two containers give roughly twice the volume for the same 41-item mix, so 0.732 is not comparable to the single-container development suite or to the official 0.505; and priority_clean_ratio ends at 0.333, so priority items are being covered even though they are routed correctly. Still unmeasured: the 80-item two-container scale the rules describe for Task A.

PHYSICS_LATERAL_GUARD (the self-imposed 10 mm on top of the official 15 mm transport clearance) is a SETTLE-SURVIVAL margin, not a search restriction, and lowering it is a regression under the shipped policy. Six scenario-matrix scenes, shipped mode, same machine: 10 mm ends 3 completed / 3 pre-check deaths, 2 mm ends 0 completed / 4 PHYSICAL settle failures (is_valid true, is_placed_safe false) / 2 pre-check -- every episode 10 mm completed becomes a physical failure at 2 mm. Paired Task B CI on the same runner generation, 3 replicates per pool, gate off: pool 10 18.00->15.00, pool 20 19.33->13.33, pool 40 20.00->16.00 placed; suite 57.33->44.33, fill 70.05->54.94, within-arm replicate spread ~0. The effect is not mediated by search volume: under the deadline 2 mm reaches MORE attempts (4518 vs 3651 per step) and MORE accepted candidates (850 vs 565) and still loses. Default reverted to 0.010; the knob remains for further study.

A POLICY_ATTEMPT_BUDGET ablation can rank arms that the shipped policy ranks the other way, because the budget puts the agent in a different operating point. POLICY_ATTEMPT_BUDGET=4000 runs ~2500 attempts/step against ~3651 under the shipped deadline -- about 30% below -- and a starved search loses episodes to physical settle failures for reasons unrelated to the arm under test (the 10 mm guard dies physically in 4 of 6 matrix scenes at budget 4000, 0 of 6 under the deadline). Both arms consumed identical work there (2496 vs 2495 attempts/step), so it was a FAIR comparison of the WRONG regime. Separately, search breadth itself is not harmful: at a fixed guard, attempts/step 1739/2558/3411 give placed 110/164/172 with physical deaths 2/4/1, monotonically better, which REFUTES the intermediate claim that more candidates make this ranker worse. Rule: run contract ablations at or above the shipped attempt rate, or in shipped mode outright.

Priority items get covered by non-priority items through the RELEASE path, closing the HANDOFF thread that suspected it. Aligning per-step priority_covered_by_other increments with the policy trace across the dual scenario-matrix scenes: 6 of 7 cover events were release actions. Mechanism: release_rest_height() treats every packed top as a landing surface and release_rejection_reason() has no support check, so planning a rest on a priority top is legal. Release is not a corner case -- about half of all shipped-mode actions are release candidates. A hard reject (RELEASE_ATTRIBUTE_GUARD=all) cuts suite priority covers 7 -> 2 but costs 47 suite placed in pi_B; restricting it to priority tops only (mode 'priority') recovers about a third of that cost (164 vs 150 vs base 197 on the comparable 7-scene subset) because the shelf scenes' binding rejections ARE priority-top rests -- late-game survival was being bought by covering priority items. Default off; the recorded next shape is a lexicographic preference (avoid covering while a non-covering candidate exists) rather than a hard reject.

submissiondeathband scored 29.959 against submissiontrueenvelope's 35.375, -15.3%, with ALL SIX components down (fill 34.246->33.635, cog 40.683->32.243, stability 53.240->41.288, placement 16.95->14.70, soft 21.30->17.45, num_placed 0.5047->0.4915). Attribution is clean: between the 35.375 artefact (3b1635c) and the submitted commit (8e29934) the only knob whose DEFAULT changes behaviour is DEATH_BAND_FALLBACK=1 -- ANCHOR_TILT_MARGIN_DEG=0 makes its shrunk() the identity, both L3 knobs are off, CONSTRUCTIVE_ORDER_MODE=composite reproduces the formula 3b1635c hard-coded, and the anchor bounds are the same half-space envelope in both. The submitted artefact DID contain the true envelope, confirmed independently by the score level itself (fill 33.6 and placed 0.4915 sit at the envelope-present level, not the pre-envelope 31.4 / 0.452). This is the first case where a local proxy (m2-k15 placed 22.0 -> 30.6) and the official score point in opposite directions.
entries.source: docs/OFFICIAL_SCORE_LOG.md; commits 3b1635c and 8e29934; user-supplied official feedback 2026-08-04 08:33:52

entries.claim: The num_placed_items gate amplifies in BOTH directions at the same rate, so any intervention that costs placed is punished several-fold in the total. trueenvelope -> deathband: placed -2.6% became -20.0% across the four gated components, a 7.6x downward factor, against the 6.7x upward factor measured on 3334 -> trueenvelope. Practical consequence: evaluate every candidate change on placed FIRST, because a change that trades a little placed for better per-placement quality has to clear roughly a 7x hurdle before it can help the total.

The implementation that produced the best official score (35.375) is NOT on the trunk. Trunk commit 050d9d7 ('trueenvelope: the total doubles') touches only docs/OFFICIAL_SCORE_LOG.md and context/evidence.json -- no agent code. Trunk's rectangular_container_anchor_bounds is still the 12-line box formula; the 68/91-line half-space version exists only on claude/l3-l4-allocation-ordering, claude/task-bottleneck-optimization-o3qtkk and claude/taskc-algorithm-improvement-ivaqo1. Measured on the bundled 000 container (width 1.45, thickness 0.04) the real y half-spaces sit at y=-0.7250 and y=+0.6850 -- ASYMMETRIC -- while the box formula assumes [-0.6850, +0.6850], so a 4 cm strip along the full 2 m length of the low-y wall is never searched even though inside_container would accept placements there. TRAP: scripts/build_submission.py packs agent/agent.py from the working tree, so rebuilding from trunk ships a pre-envelope agent (~23-point level), not the 35.375 one.
entries.source: commit 050d9d7; agent/agent.py rectangular_container_anchor_bounds on trunk vs 3b1635c; simulator/src/ground_handling/containers.py; scripts/build_submission.py

entries.claim: The scenario matrix now covers every combination axis COMPETITION_RULES section 2 declares, including the scale, after merging the trunk's matrix into the L3/L4 line and adding one scenario. The trunk's seven scenes covered containers 1/2, shelf on/off/mixed, preloaded 0/2/3 and a dedicated priority container, but every one of them reused case 000's 41-item mix, so a two-container scene arrived already half empty and allocation contention never appeared. dual-full-stream concatenates both bundled streams (83 items, indices renumbered because item['index'] is the stream identity while the action protocol's item_idx is a pool position) over two containers, one shelved, with a dedicated priority container. The bundled suite by contrast varies only the shelf axis, which is the structural reason two builds differing 15.3% officially are indistinguishable on it.
entries.source: scripts/build_scenario_matrix.py SCENARIOS; merge eb0403d; builds 8 configs verified against COMPETITION_RULES section 2

entries.claim: All six official components have a local stand-in with a published direction; only the 0-100 normalisation and the averaging weights are missing. fill and num_placed are computed by the bundled evaluator, which IS the official implementation. cog has com_z (rules: lower is better), stability has the shake metrics (rules: less movement is better), placement and soft have exact transcriptions of the covering and misrouting rules (rules: fewer violations is better). scripts/score_components.py reports these as a VECTOR and refuses to produce a total, because collapsing it requires inventing the weights -- the same act that produced the death-band regression, and the mechanism by which any optimiser, hand-written or learned, would exploit a misspecified objective. The placed gate is reported as a CONSTRAINT rather than a sixth term, matching the published rule that below a placement threshold every component except fill is zero. dominates() gives a weight-free Pareto comparison; eight tests pin that no total appears, that every entry declares direction and fidelity, that a trade dominates in neither direction, and that an unmeasured component reads None rather than zero.
entries.source: scripts/score_components.py; tests/test_score_components.py; directions from COMPETITION_RULES section 4

entries.claim: The physics-free afterstate environment enumerates ~1500 legal placements per second, but accepting them on the geometric release contract alone is not trustworthy enough to train a ranker on: across 1765 labelled release candidates in the replay dataset the weighted physically-safe rate is 0.641, the settle displacement reaches 0.373 m horizontally and 0.459 m vertically at p90, and rotation reaches 90 degrees -- so about a third of what the fast model calls legal is a pose physics rejects, and the board it predicts can be tens of centimetres from the settled one. A ranker trained there would learn to seek exactly those poses. Composing it with the risk gate the repository already ships fixes most of this without new modelling: among release candidates the gate PASSED the weighted safe rate is 0.855 (n=720) against 0.509 for those it rejected (n=1045), so the gate separates the population it was built for. Dominant rejection reasons are com_margin (968), support and overhang (882 each) and support_imbalance (330). Consequence for the RL path: the fast environment must apply the gate as part of legality, not only the geometric contract, and the residual 0.145 unsafe fraction among gate-passed poses is the fidelity ceiling any value function learned there inherits. Settled candidates are a much closer match (safe 0.860, d_xy p90 0.170, rotation p90 24.9 degrees) and are the better target if the drop model can be made to emit them.
entries.source: scripts/measure_afterstate_fidelity.py; reports/hazard/afterstate-fidelity.json; gate split computed over reports/replay-dataset

entries.claim: What predicts danger changes with how far the episode has run, which is a candidate explanation for why three global value functions all measured as noise. Stratifying the 7619-row hazard dataset by normalised episode progress: within-step discordant-pair accuracy is 0.617 fitted globally, 0.573 in the middle third, and 0.767 in the last third. Three of sixteen coefficients flip sign between regimes (attempts_consumed_log, deadline_reached, reject_corridor_frac) and several change magnitude by an order (settled_share 0.00 -> 0.56 -> 1.28; unit_coverage -0.16 -> -1.71 -> -1.47), so a single coefficient vector averages regimes whose effects partly cancel. This is a varying-coefficient / gated structure, the same shape as the Gated Iota controller that opens a geometric term only where the equivalence class is stable. IMPORTANT distinction, because it changes what is claimed: the early third has a positive rate of 0.001 and produces ZERO comparable pairs, so its unmeasurability is absent labels rather than hard prediction -- episodes do not end early. The genuine regime dependence is the sign flips and the magnitude changes, not the early-third gap. Design consequence: any board-value term should be gated to the regime where it has measured signal and closed where it has none, and the death-band gate fired without regard to regime.
entries.source: stratified refit of scripts/fit_hazard_model.py over reports/ and the scratchpad traces, 2026-08-04

entries.claim: settled_share -- the fraction of a step's search attempts spent on settled rather than release candidates -- is an observable regime variable that recovers most of the hindsight regime effect, and it passes all three checks it was designed to fail. (1) SAME-pairs LOSO comparison over 20764 within-step discordant pairs: one global coefficient vector scores 0.617, two vectors gated on settled_share score 0.679, +0.062. (2) Variable-specific, not a generic benefit of splitting: pool_size gives +0.033, release_accept_rate +0.019, while unit_coverage (-0.005), immediate_score (-0.010) and attempts_to_first (-0.011) give nothing or worse. (3) Threshold-insensitive: accuracy is 0.689/0.685/0.679/0.688 at split quantiles 0.3/0.4/0.5/0.6, degrading only at 0.7, so the boundary is not a fitted constant. It correlates +0.660 with normalised episode progress, which the agent cannot compute because it needs the terminal step, whereas settled_share is available at decision time. It is also physically interpretable: a low settled_share means the board no longer offers settled placements and the search has shifted to releases, i.e. the board is full and fragmented. This is the varying-coefficient structure the Gated Iota controller implements -- open the term where the state supports it, close it where it does not.
entries.source: stratified refits of scripts/fit_hazard_model.py, 2026-08-04: same-pairs LOSO comparison, variable sweep over eight candidate gates, threshold sweep over five quantiles

entries.claim: Both L3 allocation knobs remain inconclusive after a serial re-run on the scenario matrix, and the reason is scene bimodality rather than the knobs. On dual-dedicated-priority the identical base and base_null configs return [32,40] and [40,32]; on dual-empty they return [41,31] and [31,40] -- an 8 to 10 placed spread WITHIN one configuration, against arm deltas of +3 to +4. A noise floor computed from the difference of arm MEANS reads 0.0 there and is meaningless at n=2 when the within-arm spread is that large; the mistake is recorded because the first pass through this data reported those knobs as adoption candidates on exactly that arithmetic. The useful finding is which scene can judge: dual-full-stream (83 items over two containers, the scale COMPETITION_RULES states) returns 38 for base, base_null and l3_prefer_empty alike, so it is deterministic where the 41-item scenes are bimodal, and it is the scene worth spending repeats on. l3_release_route returned [38,28] there, one repeat of five below, which n=2 cannot separate from a single bad trajectory.
entries.source: scratchpad l3-serial/ (3 scenes x 4 arms x 2 repeats, run_queue serial)

entries.claim: The six afterstate features are one axis -- board fullness -- written six ways, and a parameter-free single feature beats the model fitted on all of them. Single-predictor AUC on the 233 labelled afterstates: occupancy_mean alone 0.944, roughness 0.872, step_index 0.846, occupancy_max 0.784, occupancy_std 0.746, while headroom_deficit (0.185) and floor_fraction_free (0.143) are simply occupancy inverted. The LOSO-fitted six-feature model scores 0.809, BELOW the raw single feature, which has no parameters to transfer and therefore no LOSO penalty -- so fitting is actively hurting through poor coefficient transfer across cases. This also explains the regime gate returning -0.004 here: gating a one-dimensional signal cannot add information. The methodological consequence is a new baseline: any proposed board feature must beat occupancy_mean's 0.944 on this target, not chance, or it is a restatement of how full the board is. What the set lacks is any quantity that varies at CONSTANT fullness -- covered voids, largest remaining free rectangle, per-type feasibility -- which is precisely what R_c in docs/theory/TASK_C_BOARD_VALUE.md was defined to measure and what could not previously be computed without generator-density contamination. The fast afterstate environment can compute it from geometry directly.
entries.source: single-feature ablation over the afterstate rows built by scripts/fit_afterstate_value.py, 2026-08-04

entries.claim: SUPERSEDES afterstate-features-are-one-axis-fullness by naming the axis correctly. The six afterstate features are not a fullness axis, they are a CLOCK. The label 'episode ends within a horizon of this step' makes step index a predictor by construction: step index alone scores AUC 0.832 on 231 rows over 8 scenario-matrix cases. Removing the within-case linear trend and level takes roughness 0.848 -> 0.439 and occupancy_mean 0.838 -> 0.549, both chance, while `placed` -- a literal step counter -- falls 0.800 -> 0.421, which is the sanity check that the residualisation works. This explains without a new hypothesis why the regime gate added nothing and why three value functions failed. NOT CONFIRMED for anything that survives: within-step pairs are ZERO for every feature because the corpus records one row per step, and residualising removes only a LINEAR clock, so a surviving residual is an upper bound. Two runs over the same eight scenes also disagree about which feature is best, so the earlier reading that R_min_type beats occupancy_mean is withdrawn.

The 'fullness-orthogonal' feature covered_void returned the SAME number as headroom_deficit to machine precision (max absolute difference 3.3e-16, Spearman 1.0). Computed from a heightmap, mean(max_height - height) IS the headroom deficit; a heightmap holds one value per column and cannot express an overhang at all. Replaced by sealed_void_fraction, which voxelises the settled AABBs and returns the shelf-sealed and item-sealed fractions separately -- an EMPTY shelf container already hides 0.268 of its interior, which belongs to the container and not to the packing.

Loading order over zones (shelf top, deep, centre, under-shelf last) is REFUTED and ZONE_ORDER ships at default off. Four scenarios, four arms, three repeats, serial, read against a POOLED base+base_null control. zone_doctrine clears the floor DOWNWARD on placed: -7.000 against a spread of 5.000 on dual-shelf-mixed, and -13.000 on single-empty-shelf where base and base_null returned identical values so the spread is degenerate at 0.000. Stability proxies move the same way (more items toppled, com_z up 0.099). zone_reversed sits at base almost everywhere, so the shipped order already beats both alternatives tested. Mechanism: filling deep and high first builds tall stacks with little under them, and a single unsafe placement terminates the episode outright. CAVEAT recorded against my own first write-up, which claimed three scenarios: under the corrected pooled control it is one solid scenario plus one degenerate.

RELEASE_ATTRIBUTE_GUARD is measured for the first time and NOT adopted, but it prices a trade nothing local could settle before. Four scenarios, three repeats, pooled control. Both arms clear the floor DOWNWARD on placed in three of four scenarios (-11.500 against a spread of 1.000 on dual-shelf-mixed). At the same time priority_covered_by_other goes to ZERO in every scenario for both arms, from 0.67-1.00 at base -- the local proxy for placement_score, the worst official component at 16.95 on a 100 scale. So the guard is a clean trade, fewer placements against no priority violations. The gate amplification argues the trade is bad, but that is an argument and not a measurement.

The four official components that exist only in the evaluation service now have locally-checkable DIRECTIONS, closing the root blocker in docs/BLOCKED_WORK.md section 0. Three reconstructible submissions spanning 23.246 to 35.375 official (base=trueenvelope, death_band=deathband, box_envelope=the 3334 level), four scenarios, three repeats, compared WITHIN each scenario against that scenario's own control. priority_covered_by_other -> placement agrees in 3 scenarios and disagrees in 0; com_z -> cog, shake_max_shift -> stability, shake_items_toppled -> stability, soft_covered_by_other -> soft and placed -> placed each agree in 1 and disagree in 0; fill is untested in all four because its spread never clears the floor. NOT ONE proxy points the wrong way. This refutes directions and fits no weights -- three points could not.

The verdict rule used by every ablation on this branch was wrong and promoted a knob that does nothing. It took floor = |base - base_null| and then measured each arm against base_null ALONE, so the same two observations set both the reference and the threshold: whichever member of the identical pair landed low became the baseline, and any arm near the other one cleared its own noise. item_cap16 read placed +6.000 CLEARS in one run and -5.000 in the next on the same scenario, while tracking base in both -- the raw repeats show base [40,40,40] / base_null [34,35,36] in the first run and base [34,35,36] / base_null [40,41,41] in the second. Corrected to a POOLED base+base_null control with the pooled spread as the floor. Under the corrected rule the attribute-guard verdict is unchanged, the zone-order verdict stands but weaker, and item_cap16 is refuted at -19.500 on dual-full-stream.

Boards do not run out of floor space, they run out of places anything would stand on. support_surfaces() admits the floor, the shelves and only PLAIN packed items, so soft and priority tops are not support. At the board c000-k1 dies on -- 16 packed, 5 soft, 3 priority -- ALL 950 legal release candidates enumerated by the deadline-free oracle rest on protected tops: rest-height support ratio median 0.000, max 0.359, zero clearing MIN_SUPPORT_RATIO 0.55, and the pose that toppled scored 0.0055. The settled contract would refuse all 950 for support; the release contract has no support test and RELEASE_ATTRIBUTE_GUARD defaults off. Neither contract matches the published rule, which penalises only DIFFERENT-attribute covering: the settled path is stricter than the rule and the release path is looser.

Connected support area above the floor is monotonically non-increasing under this candidate set, which closes the 'reward placements that create support' line. Rasterised largest-connected-face per height band over three plain-item steps and 2139 candidates: zero grow the largest elevated face, max +0.000. The reason is that support_plane_components requires THREE conditions at once -- tops within CONTACT_TOLERANCE 6 mm, lateral gap within SUPPORT_PLANE_ADJACENCY 16 mm, and overlap on the other axis. Height coincidence alone is common (345 of 1033 candidates at one step land level) and nowhere near sufficient; level AND adjacent never co-occur.

RETRACTS a claim I made and committed on this branch. The agent does NOT take dominated poses. Measured against its own candidate model with the anchor-recall oracle, at the fatal step of c000-k1: chosen pose adjusted -1.5287, best in the 950-candidate oracle -1.5301 and found_by_anytime, ZERO oracle poses beat the chosen one, reachability regret +0.0000 and ranking regret -0.0014. The retracted claim came from a 5 cm grid whose drop height was read off a heightmap; Ranker.score carries -0.18 * z * mass with masses up to 12 kg, so a sub-cell error in z moves the score by ~0.1 -- wider than the 'domination' gaps being claimed. Release recall at that step is 312 of 950 (32.8%) with zero regret, so the poses the deadline misses are ones it did not need.

A method rule, from three failures of the same family in one session. AfterstateBoard drop heights are a 5 cm lattice and must NOT be used to SCORE a pose. Ranker.score carries -0.18 * z * mass and masses reach 12 kg, so a 1 cm error in z is 0.1 of score -- most of the dynamic range that separates candidates. They remain fine for asking whether space EXISTS. Use scripts/measure_anchor_recall.py when scores must be comparable to the agent's: it enumerates from the agent's own contract and marks each candidate found_by_anytime.

The optimizer fingerprint resolves each registered knob by its ENV name, and six of sixty-eight resolved to null -- present in context/knobs.json and never actually hashed. DEATH_BAND_FALLBACK, because the variable is DEATH_BAND_FALLBACK_ENABLED, plus the five RELEASE_RISK_* thresholds, which are dataclass fields on ReleaseRiskThresholds and not module attributes at all. A knob the fingerprint cannot see is a knob a merge can change without moving the hash, which is the exact failure the registry exists to catch, and DEATH_BAND_FALLBACK is the one that cost 15.3% officially. Mirrored at module level; unhashed knobs now zero.

Scoring candidates BETWEEN the policy call and the env step changes the episode. c000-k1 ends after 21 placements with no topple under a plain replay and after 16 with a topple under a scanning one, reproducibly. The policy deadline is re-taken from perf_counter inside every policy() call so the scan steals no time, but it hammers the module-level caches the search depends on -- _cached_container_z_interval, an lru_cache of 65536, and _PACKED_AABBS_CACHE, which clears past 256 keys -- and a wall-clock-bounded search explores less from a cold cache. Record and score in two passes.

OFFICIAL RULING (SIGNATE, 2026-08-04): the shelf-height planes in PlacementValidator.check_transport_path()'s resting_surfaces and ceiling_surfaces apply REGARDLESS of require_shelf, and this is intended, not a defect. The stated reason is that require_shelf controls only the CENTRE shelf, while the left-ear small shelf always exists and divides the space, so the plane is a permanent structural constraint. resting_surfaces (thickness, height/2+thickness+buffer): a load bottom within 0-50 mm of either plane counts as a direct slide approach onto a shelf/frame top and gets NO extra lift (effective_start_z=0). ceiling_surfaces (height/2+buffer, height+buffer-thickness): the shelf underside also always acts as a clearance ceiling and clips the lift. Official advice when this causes an unwanted rejection: move the target Z by a few millimetres to leave the 0-50 mm band, or reorder the loading. VERIFIED the agent already complies: transport_sweeps() and transport_samples() apply both plane sets unconditionally, and the agent's resting plane height/2+thickness+buffer is exactly the top face of shelf_aabbs()'s small_shelf, whose generation depends on cut_x>0 and NOT on require_shelf, while main_shelf correctly does depend on the flag. DO NOT make these planes conditional; tests/test_transport_plane_contract.py pins it. NOT YET TAKEN: the agent never applies the official few-millimetre nudge, so settled candidates that land in the band are simply discarded by transport_path_clear; release candidates escape it structurally via RELEASE_TARGET_LIFT=0.052.

entries.claim: Two paired Linux shadow experiments tested the Action-Chunking-inspired delayed rollout ensemble without changing live actions. Stride 4 fixed the sparse-reach objection: scheduled proposals rose from 84/292 steps to 192/290, static-valid proposals from 48 to 148, delay-2 survival from 13.6% to 30.8%, and multi-origin-valid steps from 3 to 10. Yet not one of those steps had two delayed origins vote for the same coarse action OR the same stable item. No valid delayed proposal rescued a protocol fallback. The zero item consensus rules out an overly strict 10 cm action cell as the explanation: the deterministic greedy delayed rollouts choose different items. Therefore plain randomized-delay voting has no enforceable consensus signal in this implementation and remains OFF. Shadow placed/fill differences are not causal adoption evidence because post-selection telemetry perturbs the wall-clock-bounded trajectory.

The placement integration boundary is now explicit without changing the shipped policy: proposal facts, named immediate and release-risk evaluation, selector policy, and simulator command are separate objects. Eager rich-object construction was rejected after the first Task B parity run showed roughly 16-17% lower candidate throughput. The accepted implementation keeps rich evaluation opt-in and executes the former scalar choose/top-K loops verbatim by default. A side-by-side fixed-work check against pre-refactor commit db659b9 matched selected action, ordered top three, float-hex scores, and attempt counts exactly at budgets 128 and 512. Separate wall-clock Actions runs remain runner-noisy and are not treated as exact causal parity evidence. This is an integration seam, not evidence that a richer Ranker is beneficial.

A Ranker or selector intervention must not be adopted from placed and fill alone. Those cover only the bundled count/volume outputs, while the official score also contains CoG, stability, placement-rule, and soft-item components and uses unpublished normalizations and weights. Every paired physical ablation must therefore retain final_com_z; shake shifted fraction, topples, max shift, and peak kinetic energy; priority_clean_ratio and soft_clean_ratio; terminal inclusion/valid/safe state and failure channel; and policy time/attempt coverage alongside placed/fill. Read this as a Pareto/dominance vector and per-component regression guard, not as a fabricated local weighted total. The Task B run used during placement-pipeline refactoring was a throughput diagnostic only and cannot support selector adoption.

entries.claim: The explicit proposal/evaluation/selector/command contracts preserve the shipped policy under deterministic fixed work, but eagerly materializing rich objects for every candidate is not an admissible live measurement path. Scalar and structured evaluation matched action, ordered top three, float-hex score, and attempts exactly at budgets 128 and 512. In the 45-episode Linux physical negative control, treatment activation was confirmed on 295 of 303 decisions, yet b000-k15's six base/base_null controls were identical at placed 21 and fill 23.929 while structured_noop averaged placed 18.333 and fill 20.849; shake shifted rose 3.000 to 6.333, max shift 0.065 to 0.219, and shifted fraction 0.143 to 0.361. Priority cleanliness and terminal validity improved there, so no weighted loss is claimed; the full-vector no-op contract still failed. Policy time did not slow uniformly, so the isolated result is deadline/cache/runtime perturbation, not proof that allocation cost is the sole mechanism. Keep scalar live streaming and enrich only retained Top-K or selected candidates before testing a new Ranker.

Scalar streaming plus retained-only enrichment is an admissible live measurement boundary. It preserves candidate generation, scalar scoring and heap/incumbent updates, then constructs named proposal/evaluation/command objects only for the final decision or final Top-K. Fixed-work action, ordered Top-K, float-hex score and attempts matched exactly at budgets 128 and 512. In a 45-episode Linux physical negative control, structured telemetry appeared on 283 of 286 decisions and every per-case difference remained inside the pooled base+base_null spread across placed/fill, CoM telemetry, all shake metrics, priority/soft cleanliness, terminal inclusion/valid/safe and policy time. Attempts per decision were 8116 treatment versus 8292/8329 controls. This establishes non-interference, not policy improvement, and authorizes shadow-only multi-axis selection on the retained portfolio; eager per-candidate enrichment remains rejected.

A multi-axis instrument over retained Top-K is usable only after the live action is frozen. The pre-lookahead run 31359754451 perturbed remaining lookahead time and failed its negative control. After moving identical telemetry post-selection, every per-case metric stayed inside the pooled control spread in run 31360283401. Among 285 multi-candidate steps, 51 (17.9%) had a Pareto-dominating alternative and 14 proposed a different item. Priority/soft cover, routing, release rotation/slide risk, support, predicted CoM and scalar score stay separate; CoM is telemetry-only and no weighted total is formed.

Conservative multi-axis Pareto enforcement v1 is rejected. It made 57 substitutions only when another retained candidate dominated the final live choice on every trusted one-step rule/physical proxy. Versus the policy-matched shadow, aggregate placed was identical at 17.333, fill rose 19.921 to 20.454, priority cleanliness rose 0.850 to 0.917 and soft cleanliness 0.981 to 1.000. But b000-k20 lost 2.333 placed and 4.728 fill while topples rose 1.667 and peak kinetic energy rose 85.295; b001-k30 priority cleanliness fell 0.167; aggregate terminal validity fell 0.867 to 0.733. One-step static Pareto dominance therefore does not imply trajectory-level Pareto improvement. Keep the mode off and use paired physical replay before v2.

The first residual-state maximin sampler is a positive result for geometric dispersion but is not yet an admissible training-data sampler. In a same-snapshot paired PyBullet pilot on b000-k20 steps 3, 6 and 9, its mean observed settle-afterstate nearest-neighbour distance exceeded stratified random at all three steps by 0.022704, 0.019394 and 0.008419 (mean +0.016839). The proxy distance was also positive at all three steps. However, unique item coverage fell by 2, 1 and 1; item-orientation coverage fell by 1, 1 and 0; step 3 lost two spatial cells; and step 9 produced two fewer placed-safe replays. Therefore the descriptor can create farther-apart states, but unconstrained maximin trades away semantic item coverage and some safety. Do not train or adopt from this portfolio yet. The next sampler must guarantee item/item-orientation coverage and treat physical safety as a separate constraint before maximizing residual distance.

The second residual-state sampler enforced unseen item and item-orientation priority inside each existing kind/gate/score stratum before residual maximin. In the same-snapshot paired PyBullet pilot on b000-k20 steps 3, 6 and 9, observed settle-afterstate nearest-neighbour distance still exceeded stratified random at all three steps by 0.025438, 0.012888 and 0.005581 (mean +0.014636), and item-orientation coverage no longer regressed. It nevertheless failed the preregistered acceptance contract: global unique-item coverage was still -1 at step 3 and placed-safe replay count was still -2 at step 9. Per-stratum semantic priority cannot guarantee portfolio-wide item coverage because different strata can spend their quotas on the same item. Static semantic coverage also does not solve the late-step physical-safety selection problem. Do not train or adopt this sampler. A further dataset sampler must coordinate item coverage globally across strata and keep observed physical safety as an explicit outcome/acceptance axis rather than inferring it from the current static risk proxy.

Portfolio-wide item-to-stratum slot matching solved the semantic-coverage failure of residual diversity sampling. In the same-snapshot paired PyBullet pilot on b000-k20 steps 3, 6 and 9, the v3 portfolio beat stratified random in observed settle-afterstate nearest-neighbour distance at all steps by 0.027739, 0.058524 and 0.022009 (mean +0.036091). Global unique-item coverage improved by +1, +3 and +3, and item-orientation coverage by +4, +1 and +1. The preregistered overall verdict remains fail only because placed-safe count was 0, +1 and -1: one late-step unsafe outcome remains. The result establishes global matching as the correct semantic sampler component but not yet an admissible positive-transition training portfolio. Do not discard v3 or add another static safety gate. The next dataset stage should replay an overdrawn v3 portfolio, select the positive residual-state training arm from observed placed-safe transitions, and retain unsafe outcomes separately as negative physical-risk examples.

Observed-outcome splitting turns the globally matched residual-diversity portfolio into an admissible bounded training-data generator. With a 2x per-stratum overdraw, every candidate was replayed through the official PyBullet validator before use: placed-safe rows were globally rematched into a positive-transition arm, while unsafe rows were written separately as negative physical-risk examples. On paired b000-k20 steps 3, 6 and 9, the positive arm passed every preregistered guard. Observed settle-afterstate nearest-neighbour distance beat the safe random control by 0.030116, 0.017396 and 0.017448 (mean +0.021654); unique-item deltas were +1, +2 and +2; item-orientation deltas +4, 0 and 0; and placed-safe deltas 0, 0 and 0. The generator produced 30, 13 and 12 positive transitions and 0, 7 and 15 deduplicated negative-risk examples. This establishes the schema-v3 positive/negative dataset contract for bounded snapshots, not a learned value model or live-policy score improvement. Scale only on non-holdout states before training and retain the paired control.

entries.claim: The schema-v3 safe/risk generator executes across the core 1/2-container x shelf/no-shelf condition matrix, but command/predicted-contact residual maximin is not an unconditional physical-diversity sampler. The 2x-overdraw matrix produced 281 safe-positive and 69 negative-risk rows and passed 3/4 scenario guards; dual-empty step 15 alone had one fewer placed-safe row than its paired safe-random arm. Raising overdraw to 3x produced 282/108 rows and fixed dual-empty, but did not improve monotonically: both shelf conditions lost observed settle-afterstate NN distance at step 15 (-0.007839 dual mixed and -0.009555 single shelf), and dual mixed also lost one item-orientation. All four conditions remained physically executable and each produced a non-empty safe-positive arm. Scenario context is now explicit in every row. Do not pool conditions or tune another overdraw factor. The next dataset experiment must use observed afterstates for final portfolio selection or explicitly learn proxy fidelity, while retaining paired controls and condition-specific guards.

Replacing only the post-replay safe-positive portfolio distance with official observed x_plus afterstates removed the prior late dual-shelf proxy failure, but did not make the four-condition sampler unconditional. In frozen 3x-overdraw run 31380879143, both two-container scenarios passed. Dual-shelf-mixed step 15 improved from physical mean-NN delta -0.007839 and item-orientation delta -1 to +0.009883 and +9. The matrix nevertheless failed because single-empty-noshelf step 9 had mean-NN delta -0.004446 and single-empty-shelf step 15 had -0.017559. In both failures the minimum-NN delta remained positive (+0.002102 and +0.002309) and semantic coverage did not regress. This is no longer evidence of command-to-settle proxy error; it exposes an objective mismatch: the selector prioritizes semantic matching and greedy minimum distance, while acceptance measures mean nearest-neighbour distance against an independent control. Do not tune overdraw or train a value model yet. Seed the next positive portfolio from the paired safe control and apply observed-state swaps that preserve semantic coverage while directly improving the acceptance distance objective.

entries.claim: Seeding the safe-positive portfolio with its own paired safe-random control and then applying intra-stratum observed-afterstate swaps that keep semantic coverage and strictly raise the measured mean-nearest-neighbour delta cleared the four-condition acceptance matrix for the first time. Run 31388832646, same frozen 3x overdraw and same three steps as the failing run 31380879143, passed all four cells with per-scenario mean physical NN deltas of +0.073926 (dual-empty), +0.070353 (dual-shelf-mixed), +0.049806 (single-empty-noshelf) and +0.064257 (single-empty-shelf), and produced 307 safe-positive and 134 negative-physical-risk rows. The two previously failing single-container cells moved from -0.004446 and -0.017559 to positive. Three of the four guards are now structural rather than lucky: because the seed IS the control whenever the control fills the stratum quota, the search starts at a measured delta of exactly 0.0, the seeded portfolio is a superset of the control so unique-item and item-orientation deltas cannot be negative, and both arms are all-safe and equal size so the placed-safe delta is 0. Only the strict mean-NN guard depends on finding an improving swap. This is a dataset-coverage result: the sampled observed settle afterstates are more dispersed than an independent safe-random portfolio. It is not a live-policy, placed, fill or official-score result, and no model has been trained. The ablation arm (--observed-swap-rounds 0) has not been run in Actions, so the seeded-versus-greedy contrast rests on one matched local pair.

Four matrix runs now separate the control-seeded observed-state swap optimizer from the unseeded greedy construction it replaces, and the honest reading is narrower than 'the optimizer fixed the failing cells'. Seeded runs 31388832646 and 31389471561 both passed 4/4 (per-scenario mean physical NN deltas +0.073926/+0.070353/+0.049806/+0.064257 and +0.083348/+0.084649/+0.061929/+0.081494). The --observed-swap-rounds 0 ablation, run 31389892147 on the same commit, ALSO passed 4/4 (+0.059554/+0.022782/+0.024663/+0.031070), even though the identical greedy construction FAILED two cells in run 31380879143. The greedy arm is therefore runner-variable at the verdict level, and a single passing greedy run is not evidence that the construction is sound. Two facts survive that. First, the greedy deltas are bit-identical between 31380879143 and 31389892147 on both two-container cells (0.059554000212093394 and 0.0227817794889502) and differ only on the two single-container cells -- the same cells that failed -- so the variance is localized, not global, and this also independently confirms the ablation dispatch really ran with rounds 0. Second, every seeded per-scenario delta in both seeded runs exceeds the ablation's corresponding delta in all four cells, and the seeded arm cannot report a negative delta at all whenever the paired control fills the stratum quota, because the seed IS the control, the seeded portfolio is a superset of it, and both arms are all-safe and equal size. The optimizer's established contribution is a structural floor and a consistently larger margin, not the difference between pass and fail on any single run. Do not cite the guard verdict alone as an arm comparison; the per-scenario delta ordering and the floor are the comparable quantities.

The first learnability audit of the retained corpus returns no established signal. On 325 modelable rows across 11 states and 4 cases from run 31391424126, with a leave-one-case-out split and ranking measured inside each state, the incumbent Ranker.score has the best mean within-state AUC for is_placed_safe at 0.768. A numpy logistic model on the eight-scalar phi_modelling vector reaches 0.741 and a quantile-cell lookup 0.564, against 0.500 for a constant. The linear model does take the safe candidate more often at top-1 (0.900 versus 0.800), but on 10 usable states that is one state of difference and is not a result. Settle regression is weakly positive and not more: leave-one-case-out R-squared against a held-out constant is 0.141 for delta_theta_deg and 0.075 for d_norm with the linear model, while the lookup table is worse than the constant (-0.121 and -0.082). The audit is instrumented to be able to say yes: on a synthetic corpus with a planted feature-0 signal it returns signal_beyond_incumbent with within-state AUC above 0.8, and on matched pure noise it returns no signal. Scope limits are real and bound the conclusion. Only release candidates carry a feature vector, so 117 settled-candidate rows have no phi at all and were excluded; the safe/unsafe mixture is a sampling design, so no calibration claim is made; and only numpy is available, so GBDT and Deep Sets from the keystone plan were NOT run and this bounds them weakly. The actionable reading is that eight static contact scalars do not beat the existing scalar score at ranking one-step physical safety on four cases, and that more distinct states, not more rows per state, is what would make a stronger test possible.

entries.claim: Widening the matrix from four scenarios and three steps to eight scenarios and six steps took the retained corpus from 11 states over 4 cases to 49 distinct boards over 8 cases (1778 modelable rows), and re-running the learnability audit at that size sharpens the picture without changing the verdict. On leave-one-case-out with ranking measured inside each board, the incumbent Ranker.score still leads for is_placed_safe: mean within-state AUC 0.745 and top-1 safe rate 0.872, against 0.727/0.851 for a logistic model on the eight contact scalars, 0.671/0.780 for a quantile lookup, and 0.500/0.683 for a constant. The verdict stays no_established_signal for safety ranking. What did change is the settle regression, which improved consistently with data: leave-one-case-out R-squared against a held-out constant went from 0.141 to 0.184 for delta_theta_deg and from 0.075 to 0.125 for d_norm with the linear model, while the lookup table went from worse than a constant (-0.121 and -0.082) to positive (0.075 and 0.078). That is the signature of a data-starved estimator becoming viable, and it says the usable signal in Phi is about how far and how much an item settles, not about which candidate is safe. Two measurement corrections are folded in. Boards shared by more than one run are now deduplicated in the audit as they already were in the corpus index, which removed 241 rows and, with them, the apparent top-1 edge the logistic model had at 0.870 against 0.852; that edge was double-counted boards. And a scenario whose episode ends before the last requested step is no longer treated as a broken dataset, which had been silently dropping two of eight scenarios from the matrix verdict and capping the step axis.

The learnability learning curve saturates at roughly 16 training states, so more states is not the constraint and the earlier time-to-target extrapolation is withdrawn. Sweeping the number of training boards on the 93-board corpus (leave-one-case-out, sampling by state because rows inside a state are not independent) gives mean within-state AUC 0.666, 0.697, 0.710, 0.708, 0.711, 0.711 at 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 and 78 states, and R-squared for delta_theta_deg of -0.008, 0.055, 0.153, 0.148, 0.166, 0.164 over the same sweep. From 16 states to 78 -- nearly five times the data -- AUC moves by 0.001 and the regression by 0.011. The incumbent Ranker.score sits at 0.745 and is not approached. An earlier fit over 8 to 40 states measured +0.0107 AUC per doubling and was used to project parity near 200 states and AUC 0.80 near 7000; the full curve shows that slope was the estimator climbing out of the data-starved regime below 16 states, not a trend, and those projections are withdrawn. What binds is the feature set and the target, not the row count: eight static contact scalars describing one candidate carry what they carry. Collecting more boards is still worth doing for coverage of conditions the corpus lacks, but it should not be justified as a route to a better model on this feature set.

entries.claim: A model trained on the board beats the incumbent Ranker.score at ranking one-step placement safety, and the earlier 'no signal / saturates at sixteen boards' conclusion is withdrawn: it was a property of the eight-scalar contact vector, not of the data. On the same 3482 rows, 93 boards and 8 cases, with the identical protocol (leave-one-case-out, ranking scored inside each board, an assertion that no board straddles a fold), mean within-state AUC for is_placed_safe is 0.725 for the incumbent, 0.709 for a linear model on the eight scalars, 0.770 for the SAME eight scalars with a small MLP, 0.851 for an MLP that also sees the candidate's own geometry and its container, and 0.830 for set attention over the placed items and pending pool. Top-1 safe rate follows the same order: 0.867, 0.868, 0.876, 0.967, 0.944. Two attributions follow from the arm design. Model capacity alone already beats the incumbent, so the audit's linear arm was under-powered rather than the features being empty. The largest single jump is 0.770 to 0.851 on adding the candidate's own position, size, orientation and container geometry -- information phi_modelling never carried, since it describes predicted contact and never says where in the container the item is going. Attention over the board does NOT help safety ranking, coming in below the plain candidate MLP, but it does help the settle regression: leave-one-case-out R-squared against a held-out constant is 0.322 versus 0.277 for delta_theta_deg and 0.382 versus 0.345 for d_norm, against 0.147 and 0.081 for the audit's linear arm. So the board predicts how far an item settles; the action's own geometry predicts whether it is safe. This is a dataset-level ranking result on 8 cases with 2 seeds. It is not a live-policy result: the incumbent is consumed inside a deadline-bounded search, and this project has already rejected selectors that looked better statically and lost on trajectories (multi-axis Pareto enforce v1). Read the ordering of the arms, not the third decimal.

The state model's advantage over the incumbent reproduces on a larger corpus and survives the obvious leak. Both arms were trained on a frozen copy of the same 130 boards over 8 cases, which matters because CI lands boards continuously and two earlier attempts compared 93 boards against 118 without noticing. With all positives (4955 rows): mean within-state AUC 0.733 incumbent, 0.767 phi_mlp, 0.842 candidate_mlp, 0.835 set_attention. With the positives restricted to the stratified-random control arm (2926 rows), which removes the observed-state swap optimizer's diversity selection from the safe class: 0.745, 0.768, 0.851, 0.841. The ordering is identical and the candidate MLP's margin over the incumbent is if anything larger once the selection is removed, so the model is not reading the sampler. That is now six measurements -- three corpus sizes at 93, 118 and 130 boards, two positive sources -- all with the same ordering. Top-1 safe rate is the metric that moves between arms (0.969 against 0.882 for the candidate MLP), because it depends on the safe fraction per board, which is a sampling design; AUC is the rank measure to quote. Attention again loses to the plain candidate MLP on safety ranking and wins on the settle regression, where it is the best arm on both targets in both sources (R-squared 0.337 and 0.390 with all positives, 0.299 and 0.373 with control only, against the audit linear arm's 0.147 and 0.081). Still not a live-policy result: the incumbent is consumed inside a deadline-bounded search, latency is unmeasured, and a selector that looked better statically has already lost on trajectories here (multi-axis Pareto enforce v1). The next gate is a physical negative control, not another dataset run.

The residual-diversity metric was applied across two coordinate frames and nobody had checked what that cost. `state-NNN.json` states the contract: `candidate_positions` are container-local, `packed_item_positions` are world, and the replayed `x_plus` position is world. So the overdraw stage scores container-local commands and the final observed stage scores world settled positions, and on a two-container board those frames differ by the container spacing -- measured at 2.5 m against item extents of tens of centimetres. Consequences: a cross-container pair saturates the normalised position term whatever the items did, container membership is counted twice (once by that offset, once by the `container_index` categorical), and the command proxy has the opposite bug, seeing two candidates at the same local spot in different containers as nearly identical. Measured on 454 retained boards by shifting settled x and y back into their own container's frame -- not z, because a commanded 0.227 settling to 0.175 is the item dropping five centimetres, not a frame difference. The optimizer's gain against its paired control is +0.074200 as reported and +0.071780 in one frame; on the 294 multi-container boards, +0.075168 against +0.071431, positive on every one of them in both frames. The 160 single-container boards are bit-identical by construction, which is the control on this control. So the defect is real and must be fixed in `settled_proxy_record`, but it is NOT the explanation for the observed-state swap optimizer's margin: the margin survives collapsing the frames, losing about 3 percent of its size.

The single Gower sum answers two different questions at once and cannot say which one moved. Placing a candidate occupies a region of a container AND consumes an item, leaving a different pool behind; two placements can match on one and differ on the other. The weighting was never chosen either: each categorical field contributes a full 1.0 while a normalised position difference contributes a fraction, so on observed records -- where only centre, size and settle tilt survive -- four of eleven terms are discrete identity. Measured: identity alone reproduces 0.793 of the full metric's 0.839 mean within-board rank agreement, so most of the ordering is discrete. Splitting the sum into an occupancy component (centre, size, settle tilt, container_index) and a consumption component (pool_index, item_index) and re-scoring the optimizer against its paired control in the corrected frame on 454 boards: mean delta occupancy +0.049909 with 452 wins, 0 ties, 2 losses; mean delta consumption +0.095786 with 294 wins, 81 ties, 79 losses. Both components are positive independently, so the optimizer is not winning one axis by sacrificing the other -- but consumption is much noisier, and the ties are boards where both arms drew the same item set, not boards the optimizer lost. The fix is to report the two components and stop fabricating a total, which is the rule the multi-axis selector already follows.

A learned residual space does not yet beat the fourteen hand-made proxy fields at ordering candidate-versus-candidate afterstate difference, but the evidence is weaker than the headline. On 105108 within-board pairs from 130 boards over 8 cases, leave-one-case-out, against truth = the same Gower distance the acceptance guard reports on observed x_plus: command_proxy 0.839 mean within-board Spearman, candidate_mlp 0.432, set_attention 0.472. Read the decomposition before the headline, because the comparison is not fair to the learned arms: the proxy and the truth share their four categorical fields, so part of command_proxy's agreement is tautological. Identity alone scores 0.793 and geometry alone 0.658, and geometry-versus-geometry -- the only comparison with no shared terms on either side -- is 0.659. So the honest statement is that the proxy's geometry predicts the truth's geometry at about 0.66 and the learned arms have not been measured against that number on equal terms. This is why the same models beat the incumbent on safety ranking (0.842 within-state AUC against 0.733) yet lose here: the two tasks are different, and this one is scored against a metric that is 79 percent discrete identity. Do not read this as 'do not train a transformer'. It says the current residual metric is not a good target to learn, which is a statement about the metric.

The coordinate-frame defect is fixed at the source and the fix moves the metric in the intended direction. `settled_proxy_record` now takes `container_offsets` and `build_replay_dataset` derives them once from the observation and passes them to both the outcome split and the acceptance guard, so the swap search, the guard and the coverage report read a single frame; x and y are shifted and z is not, because a commanded z of 0.227 settling to 0.175 is the item dropping five centimetres. Omitting the argument still reproduces the world-frame descriptor, so every measurement recorded before 2026-08-11 stays readable. Measured as a paired comparison -- the same trained embeddings scored against the truth in both frames, 140456 within-board pairs from 171 boards over 8 cases, so the frame is the only thing that differs: commanded geometry against settled geometry, the one comparison with no shared terms on either side, rises from 0.658 to 0.686 mean within-board Spearman; geometry-only proxy against the full truth rises from 0.665 to 0.708; identity-only falls from 0.787 to 0.747. That is the fix working: the 2.5 m offset was inflating the discrete half of the metric by double-counting container membership, and removing it shifts weight onto actual geometry. The learned arms are unmoved (candidate_mlp 0.469 to 0.460, set_attention 0.494 to 0.498), so the frame was never what was holding them back. Guard deltas from runs before commit 2ccb262 are in the old frame and must not be compared directly against later ones on multi-container boards; single-container boards are unaffected by construction. The second defect is NOT fixed: the search still maximises the single sum.

Re-measured in the corrected coordinate frame on a larger corpus, a learned residual space still does not beat the fourteen hand-made proxy fields at ordering candidate-versus-candidate afterstate difference -- and one number in the superseded entry was glossed wrongly. On 140456 within-board pairs from 171 boards over 8 cases, leave-one-case-out, truth = the Gower distance over settled x_plus in the container frame: command_proxy 0.844 mean within-board Spearman, candidate_mlp 0.460, set_attention 0.498. THE CORRECTION: the superseded entry called this 'a metric that is 79 percent discrete identity'. That is wrong. 0.793 was a Spearman rank correlation between the identity-only proxy and the truth, not a share of the metric. The correct statements are two: four of the eleven terms present on observed records are categorical, and the identity-only proxy alone reaches 0.747 rank agreement against the full metric's 0.844 -- so the discrete half carries most of the ordering, but no percentage of the metric is attributable to it and none should be quoted. The rest of the reading stands and is now firmer: the proxy and the truth share their four categorical fields, so part of command_proxy's agreement is tautological, and the only comparison with no shared terms on either side is commanded geometry against settled geometry, at 0.686. That is the number the learned arms should be judged against, and they have still not been measured against it on equal terms. This is why the same models beat the incumbent on safety ranking (0.842 within-state AUC against 0.733) yet lose here: the tasks are different. Do not read this as 'do not train a transformer'.
