entries.claim: Refusing a component-degrading swap buys consumption diversity and costs the single sum, measured as a within-board paired comparison. The dataset builder runs two optimizers on every board -- same pool, same seed, same forced keys, only the acceptance rule differs -- so the difference is the rule and not the board. That pairing is not optional: the policy is deadline-limited, two runs of one scenario do not reach the same board, and the earlier greedy-versus-seeded verdict turned out to be runner-variable for exactly that reason. On 44 boards from matrix run 31491047020: the question is live, because the shipped sum rule accepted 171 swaps that raised the sum while a component fell, on 40 of the 44 boards. Gate minus sum, with an exact two-sided sign test on the paired boards: consumption +0.029919 mean, 25 boards better / 15 tied / 4 worse, p=0.0001 -- a real gain, raising mean consumption delta from 0.095 to 0.125. Occupancy +0.001921 mean, 24 / 7 / 13, p=0.0989 -- INDISTINGUISHABLE, and reporting it as a win on the strength of the mean sign was a mistake the instrument now refuses to make. The single Gower sum falls by 0.005548, 2 / 6 / 36, p<0.0001, which is expected by construction because the gate refuses moves the sum rule would take; that row is a check that the arms differ, not a result. Adoption is safe on the guard: the acceptance test reads the sum, and its minimum over the 44 boards falls only from 0.035931 to 0.030851, with no board at or below zero under either rule. So the honest summary is that the gate improves the component nobody was watching, does not measurably move the one they were, and pays for it in a number whose weighting nobody chose.

The acceptance-gate result reproduces on 46 fresh boards with the two rules in the opposite slots, and this is also the adoption's negative control. Run 31492719115 ships pareto_gate and shadows sum; run 31491047020 did the reverse. Gate minus sum, second run against first: consumption +0.033687 against +0.029919, 25/15/6 against 25/15/4, sign-test p=0.0009 against p=0.0001; occupancy +0.001274 against +0.001921, 25/7/14 against 24/7/13, p=0.1081 against p=0.0989 -- indistinguishable in both, which is the honest call and not a win; the single sum -0.004560 against -0.005548, expected by construction. Same verdict string from an instrument that had no way to know which run it was reading. The condition matrix passes 8/8 with the gate shipped, 985 safe-positive and 548 negative-risk rows, and the guard number's minimum is 0.033627, clear of zero. ONE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN THE INSTRUMENT: scripts/measure_swap_acceptance.py keyed the two arms by slot rather than by the acceptance rule each ran, so the moment adoption swapped the slots every column came out sign-flipped and mislabelled -- the replicated consumption win first printed as 'sum_better'. It now reads each trace's own `acceptance` field, and a test drives the same fixture through both slot assignments and asserts the answer does not move. The pre-adoption entry's numbers were computed before the swap and are unaffected.

The caveat is dead: the learned arms lose the residual-space comparison on equal terms, not merely on a rigged one. Every predictor was previously scored against the full Gower sum, which contains four categorical fields the hand-made proxy carries verbatim -- the proxy was handed what the learned arms had to earn. Splitting the metric made the fair version available. On 162978 within-board pairs from 182 boards over 8 cases, leave-one-case-out, 200 epochs, in the corrected container frame, scored against the OCCUPANCY half of the truth alone (where the item actually settled, the part physics decides): command_proxy 0.709, command_proxy_geometry_only 0.667, set_attention 0.502, candidate_mlp 0.491. The unfair advantage was real but small: the gap shrinks from 0.344 on the full sum to 0.207 on occupancy, and the proxy still wins decisively. Even geometry alone, with no discrete term shared with anything, beats the best learned arm by 0.165. Two supporting reads. The learned arms barely move between the full truth and the occupancy truth (0.477 to 0.491, 0.504 to 0.502), so they were never collecting the categorical part; and they score 0.175 and 0.165 against the consumption half, confirming that column is definitional for the proxy rather than predictive. A diagnostic: the full sum's own ordering correlates 0.917 with its occupancy half and 0.422 with its consumption half, so every verdict previously read off the sum was mostly a verdict about occupancy that did not say so. THE LIMIT OF THIS RESULT, which must not be dropped when it is cited: the learned arms were trained on safety classification and settle regression, and their EMBEDDINGS were read out and scored here. No model has ever been trained directly on the residual-distance target. So this says embeddings trained for safety ranking do not transfer to ordering residual difference. It does not say a learned residual space is unreachable, and it is not grounds to stop building one.

The bounded multi-step graph instrument can reconstruct independent physical branches and preserve a non-degenerate H3/B2 tree deterministically on one Task B development root. On b000-k20 step 3 it produced 1/2/4/8 nodes by depth and 14 physically safe edges spanning five stable items. Two same-commit runs produced byte-identical graph JSON, IDs and SHA256. This validates the instrument on one early root only; it does not establish learnability, mid/late coverage, or failure-label coverage.

The first eight-condition H3/B2 physical matrix establishes bounded residual/failure signal but not training readiness. It completed all requested conditions with 51 edges (47 safe, 4 physical failures) and 32 terminal trajectories (23 horizon, 5 no-candidate, 4 physical-failure). Eight unequal-immediate-score sibling pairs had different downstream ranges; in bounded reachability, a lower-score action could still produce a better leaf on fill, CoG, surface variation, or soft coverage. None of the 15 exact-score sibling ties separated on the recorded axes. Therefore H5 and value-model training remain gated on a larger replicated H3 set and held-out separation.

The expanded H3/B2 matrix preserved immediate-score-order counterexamples across a preregistered root-step split, but exact-score ties remained uninformative at H3. Run 31558667741 completed 24 roots across all 8 conditions with 207 edges and 127 terminal trajectories. Both discovery step<15 and late holdout step>=15 contain lower-score branches with better reachable leaves. None of 42 exact-score sibling pairs differed on recorded downstream ranges; raw-graph inspection also found no difference in leaf count, maximum depth, or terminal-reason multiset. Training remains gated. Only a targeted H5 diagnostic on root-level exact ties is justified; broad H5 generation and value-model training are not.

Exact immediate-score ties did not become informative when three root-level H3 ties were selectively extended to H5/B2. Run 31559232452 completed all three graphs at the full 63-node/62-edge bound: 186 safe edges and 96 horizon leaves. Across 39 exact-score sibling pairs, zero differed on the recorded downstream ranges. This rejects the narrow hypothesis that H3 alone hid the tie signal on these roots. The informative H3 supervision is therefore exported as 52 discovery plus 9 late-holdout multi-axis pair rows, while 42 exact/outcome-identical pairs remain separate controls. The export is not model-ready because source-state feature tensors are not yet attached.

The 116-feature label-blind local-geometry pre-action family is rejected with adequate power. V5 refit the v4 kNN protocol on all 29 opened runs (14 streams, 1053 exact signatures) and scored 719/1053 versus 657/1053 in strict group-complement cross-fit (127 wins/65 losses, p=9.05e-6, 14/14 streams non-regressing), then carried a frozen power gate: the prospective sign test may only be opened at 37+ discordant pairs, countable label-blind because differing binary directional predictions make exactly one system correct. The first seed-60 cohort (8 completed streams, 27 disagreements) was detected as underpowered without opening labels; after a second label-blind wave, 12 completed streams reached 42 disagreements and the single evaluation opened: 161/229 versus 157/229, 23 wins/19 losses, p=0.644, three streams regressing. The development cross-fit advantage (0.661 win fraction) did not transfer (0.548). Third consecutive new-stream failure for this representation (v3 linear seed-58, v4 kNN seed-59 underpowered, v5 kNN seed-60 powered); do not retune the same features into a v6. The powered-gate protocol worked and carries forward.

The stamped-height-grid pre-action representation is rejected in development without spending a confirmation stream. On all 41 opened runs (26 streams, 5338 rows, 1751 exact signatures) under the unchanged v4/v5 protocol, no policy in the 288-point kNN grid was non-regressing across all streams. The pooled-best policy scored 1191/1751 versus action geometry 1121/1751 (203 wins/133 losses, p=1.6e-4) but regressed five streams, worst on the structured variants interleave (48 vs 55) and reverse-000 (61 vs 66), and its 0.604 win fraction would demand 92 discordant pairs for a powered confirmation. A pooled sign test that hides stream-level regressions is exactly what the non-regression precondition exists to catch. The pre-action branch-direction question stays open with no live candidate; the next attempt must model arrival-order structure or change the label target, not re-tune this grid.

The one-episode suggestion that the live immediate-Q ordering is actively wrong over long horizons (concordance 0.267 on 15 decided pairs) does not replicate at five-config scale and the sign reverses. Actions run 31931772512 ran the branch-label instrument on b000-k15/k20/k40 and b001-k20/k30 at six branch steps with class-diverse top-3 siblings and schema-2 per-sibling RankEvaluation components; 25 valid states and 59 usable branches survived the prefix/parent-fingerprint filters. Live-q concordance with final fill is 27/39 (0.692, exact two-sided p=0.0237) and with final placed 19/30 (p=0.20); the top-q sibling reaches the best outcome in 15/25 and 15/23 states. A leave-one-config-out ridge reweighting of the same components loses held-out (19/39 fill, 10/30 placed), so the shipped scalar is not beatable by re-mixing its own terms on this corpus. Do not launch an episode-level weight sweep on the old 0.267 signal; the full-data fit's negative support weight is hypothesis-generating only. Pairs within a state share history; the per-state top-pick rows are the conservative reading.

entries.supersedes_reason: the b-config replication weakened the single-run concordance claim and the fatal-case extension found a significantly inverted regime
entries.claim: The live immediate-Q ordering is regime-dependent, and the regime where it is significantly anti-predictive is exactly the certified-fatal pool-1 case with large avoidable losses. Run 31938388838 extended branch labels to c000-k1/c001-k1 at steps 2-20 with same-item top-candidate siblings and a per-sibling support-surface ledger, and re-ran the five b-configs as an independent replication. c001-k1 is intrinsic: in 0/9 measurable states does any sibling beat the policy on final placed, extending the step-18 choice-invariant ceiling back to step 2 -- not suicide. c000-k1 is avoidable: 6/8 states had a strictly better sibling (a single different placement at step 8 ends 6 placements higher; step 16, 5 higher) and the higher-q sibling reaches the better ending in only 3/17 pairs on placed (p=0.0127) and 3/18 on fill (p=0.0075) -- the q tiebreak among the policy's own top-3 candidates is systematically wrong there. The b replication gave fill 24/41 and placed 13/32 versus the prior run's 27/39 and 19/30; pooled over both runs fill is 51/80 (p=0.0183) and placed 32/62 (p=0.90), so the earlier single-run refutation is rescoped: mildly concordant on fill, no signal on placed, deadline-sensitive instrument. The support ledger is directional only (usable-support delta 4/4 comparable fill pairs, p=0.125). This licenses a scoped pool-1 selection experiment and a mechanism-first look at the inverted pairs; it does not license touching the live ranker globally.

The c000-k1 q-ordering inversion is a single-deviation property and does not compose into a policy. The mechanism audit found no single axis behind the inverted pairs: the micro q-differences (mostly |dq|<=0.055) point the wrong way through different components at different steps (lateral at steps 2/8, depth at 4/10, lift at 6). A driver-side causality probe on c000-k1 (agent untouched) forced, at every step, either the highest-q or lowest-q member of the deterministic budget-4096 spatially-distinct top-3: live policy 23 placed/26.10 fill in 24 steps; per-step top-q 18/16.16 in 19 steps; per-step min-q collapsed to 10/6.96 in 11 steps. Wholesale inversion is catastrophic, and even the top-q arm loses five placements to the live deadline search while agreeing with it on 16/19 steps, so offline-reconstruction selectors carry a built-in handicap that any future experiment must control with exactly this arm. Harvesting the real avoidable losses requires a selective state-conditional deviation, which needs the still-missing regime detector; the q-margin alone does not transfer (b-case small-gap pairs are concordant 17/22 while c-case small-gap pairs are 11/29). Single local Linux machine, one episode per arm, no repeats: directional development evidence.

Crossing all 51 schema-2 anchor-recall oracle states with their decision-time policy telemetry yields a four-phase feasibility structure and a first in-search phase detector. Phases: P0 found (26 states / 9 distinct boards), P1 deadline-miss (17/8: live-generator-reachable settled candidates exist, none accepted), P3 true-empty (8/2), and P2 generator-hole occurs zero times -- the support-plane generator always covers part of any nonempty settled set, so live settled failure is either drowning or vacuum, never coverage. Two properties of the transition: it is trajectory-endogenous (the same case-step coordinate spans oracle 0 to 798 settled across agent generations, so the cliff moves with policy quality and is not a fixed property of the case), and near the cliff the candidate space implodes, which makes the scan finish. That yields the detector: zero settled accepted AND scan-unit completion >= 1/3 calls true-empty with precision 1.0 and recall 7/8 on raw states (1.0 and 1/2 on distinct boards; the single miss is the oldest pre-improvement run's board at 2/120 units). Drowning states never complete a third of their units (max 16/120) because their spaces are huge (support-plane-reachable 72-962). All quantities in the rule are in policy_log at decision time. Caveats: two cases only, heavy replicate structure (19 distinct boards), the board-level recall rests on two true-empty boards. This is the instrument-validated seed of a regime detector, not an adopted policy input.

The vacuum cutoff is rejected at its preregistered development gates, and the failure mode is general: a post-hoc phase classifier does not survive being used as an in-flight stopping rule. VACUUM_SETTLED_CUTOFF=0.34 skipped remaining settled units once a third exhausted with zero settled candidates, reallocating the deadline to release units. Paired run 31941364445 (4 cases x 2 arms x 3 replicates): c000-k1 tied at 18.33 mean placed (same outcome multiset, runner timing shuffles which replicate reaches 23); c001-k1 collapsed uniformly 21->16, every replicate trading a late transport_invalid ending for an earlier topple; paired placed 2 wins/7 losses. The predicted benefit did appear -- transport_invalid endings fell 5->1 and bundled valid rate rose 0.583->0.917 -- but it was bought by abandoning settled placements the shipped policy was still finding, which is the wrong exchange everywhere the rule fired. The classifier's precision 1.0 was measured on finished searches; an early-stop rule's false-fire cost is invisible to that metric, and full settled exhaustion, the sound version of this trigger, is already handled by anchor_fallback. The knob stays registered at default 0 (behaviour_sha256 unchanged) solely to reproduce this result. Any future in-flight regime controller must measure its false-fire cost in-flight and carry these paired no-harm controls from the start.
